svg.title: How refine and translate rewrite a transcript
svg.desc: One stretch of speech, drawn as a waveform over its eight caption lines with chapter marks for Intro and Results, leaves two ways. With the timestamps flag, each line is rewritten in its own slot and keeps its timing, the filler words the model dropped shown struck through; where the reply has no ID for line 7, line 6 spans both slots. By default the lines regroup into five sentences; the model marks where the talk turns and which sentence really opens the Results chapter, one line earlier than its timestamp; the sentences become three paragraphs, rewritten whole and set under the chapter titles as an article. Every request on both routes carries the title, description, and repeated names, neighbouring lines for context, and numbered lines; replies open each line with its ID, and a reply missing one is asked again. A playhead plays across the lines and starts over, outlining the line, reply, sentence, and paragraph under it and highlighting that paragraph on the page.

g.text: WHAT WAS SAID, AND ITS CAPTION LINES
line by line: each reply goes back into its own line's slot
We ran ten tests and all passed.
no [LINE7] came back, so [LINE6] spans both slots
struck words are the filler the model dropped
an article: lines regroup into sentences, then paragraphs under the chapter titles
the model marks the turns, and the sentence that opens each chapter
So today we'll see how it reads files. And it chunks.
Next: results. We ran ten tests and all passed.
